The locals had something to think about when Green and Fletcher came round the last corner side by side in faultless style. The race was a great one to watch, our first pair going away from the field of over 200, and deserving all the good things said about them at the finish.

McMullen, Hyde, Pope, Scammel, Green, Fletcher and Holland, were the most prominent. The race proceeded with the first position undecided and not until two miles from home could Green, Pope and Hyde shake off the others.

Looking through the list of sufferers, one sees such names as McMullen and Odell (Irish); Williams, Davis, Davies, Thomas and Powell (Welsh); Fletcher, Mitchell, Crighton, Stewart and McKay (Scotch); and Merlin (Cornish).

The two-mile walk handicap served to show Len Fletcher's excellent form. 14min. 21 3-5 secs. from scratch on a May evening, should lead to something even better on a warm afternoon in July; possibly an A.A.A.
Manning and Wattam pleased the crowd, as also did Bidgood. Fletcher came along in the last group, smiling and determined. Having seen all that was wanted, the 'bus continued its journey.

In both cases they had a dour, side-by-side struggle throughout; and all of this was provided for us again by Len Fletcher and Tommy Green in this year's race.

Hyde, the A.A.A. seven miles champion, by our champion, Len Fletcher. Len led at two miles, was over fifty yards behind at seven miles, and yet won by over two minutes, recording 83 mins. 46 secs. for the 10½ miles—surely his best performance yet.
The next race was at the normal track distance of 2 miles, and Len Fletcher, fresh from victory in the London Business Houses Championship, sportingly obliged by turning out for the club.
Fletcher was not severely pushed, he finished in good time; in fact only five seconds slower than his championship record of 1927.
There came a time when so much talking must have made him thirsty, for he started to run faster, shouting out something about a pint of beer and Fletcher.
Canard, Chorley, Fletcher, and a newcomer in Carter, all ran prominently and should still further improve on their positions in future races.

Runners passed by until Fletcher came along, 30th, and Canard, 37th; Chorley and Coleman were still further behind, and as Mitcham and Reading's fourth man had already passed it did not look any too rosy for the Bels.

However, Len Fletcher again followed Hyde home, and led our team to their third scratch team win. Frank Thorn showed a return to form in finishing fifth and was our second man home.

The same course as last year was used and Hyde, Fletcher and Pope took the lead in turn. They were still together with Fletcher, if anything, a yard in front, when Hyde suffered disqualification for the second year in succession.

Fletcher and Robertshaw, who had started slowly were now gaining much ground and many places. Nearing the finishing post, Cohen led Allum by fifty yards and Arthur made a desperate spurt to try and gain the tape but was beaten by half-a-dozen yards or so, with Penny a hundred yards in the rear, followed by Jack Flower.
Next we have Bert Smith at last prepared to "do or die," with "Nobby" Fletcher at his heels. Hello! here comes the "three starred nap," Tom Cotton, in quite a hurry.
Had he returned this time in the former race he would have been placed 4th, after Fletcher, Pope and Tommy Green. Moreover, his time was 1¾ min. faster than Frank Elson's when winning last year.
Carter, who came next, ran a good steady race, but dropped a couple of places in the second lap, which Fletcher picked up and finished close behind.
In addition, Harry Larman, a persevering and improving walker, was placed second in the individual handicap. With Fletcher (1st) beating C.

Fletcher, whose improved and consistently good walking has proved a feature of this season. Green, however, decided that Len would have to earn his championship medal, and never left Fletcher's shoulder until the last half mile.
Fletcher, the County champion, and Thorn, both suffered disqualification and this put paid to our hopes of winning the championship for the first time.

The programme also included a 2 miles Team Walk to which we received an invitation, together with Woodford Green A.C., Enfield A.C., Highgate H., Surrey A.C. and the promoting club, Polytechnic H., Hyde, of Enfield, won, followed by Cooper and Pope, of Woodford Green, and Fletcher, of our Club.
Fletcher retained his title of London Business Houses Walk Champion, and T.
Fletcher has been in a class by himself in the Club as a track walker, and he had little strong opposition in the Walking Championship, retaining his title with ease.

Fletcher had an uneasy time in the early stages of the race, but recovered later and did well to finish fifth. Enfield team again succeeded in winning the scratch team event, this time by 24 pts. to our 30 pts.

They were Hyde (Enfield A.C., scratch), and our own Fletcher (20 secs.) and Green (30 secs.). Our return fixture with the Police Walkers was held over our “Open” seven miles course, and scoring 15 aside resulted in a win for us. Fletcher led throughout, Field managed to beat P.C. Caffrey for second place and Redgrave did well to finish fourth.

Both have given us scratch team wins and in both races Len Fletcher has been the individual winner. In the race at Bellingham, Fletcher beat Hyde in convincing fashion, and our scratch team finished 1, 5, 6 and 7—most satisfactory.

Unfortunately, Tommy Green, whose unavailing but closely fought races with Len Fletcher in the last two races for the Club title at this distance are so well remembered, was unable to compete owing to an attack of influenza.

With Carter, Shields, Shaw, Mains, Rice, Mitchell (A.F.), Walker, Fletcher and others our team looks good. Also the "Sir Jeremiah Colman" Cup for the first team to finish 12 men (which we hold) must be retained.

The time of the winner was 9 mins. 43 secs., and considering the heavy going this was quite a sound performance. In the 3 Miles Walk we saw a fine performance by Len Fletcher who, off 20 yds., finished second to L.
The annual contest for the right to hold the "Murphy" Shield for the ensuing year attracted a fair field, including a past holder in Len Fletcher, and the holder, Don Brown.

Pope, Fletcher and Wright preferred to start comparatively slowly, and speed up as the race progressed. Churcher walked strongly throughout and dropping his opponents, won fairly easily from Bidgood and Bentley, who were to fight out the Police Long Distance Championship on the following Thursday.

Churcher, Fletcher, Green, Harley, Readman and Rickards, should be our team. Unfortunately, Fletcher was indisposed, Green was unable to turn out, and Rickards was also compelled to stand down at the last moment.
